prompt: Write `truncate_to_budget(messages, budget, count)`. `messages` is a list of {"role","content"}; `count(msg)` returns its token cost. Keep ALL system messages, then keep as many of the NEWEST non-system messages as fit in the remaining budget (contiguous from the end, never skipping a message to fit an older one), preserving original order. Python code block only.
tests:
cnt = lambda m: len(m["content"])
ms = [{"role":"system","content":"sss"},{"role":"user","content":"aaaa"},{"role":"assistant","content":"bb"},{"role":"user","content":"c"}]
assert truncate_to_budget(ms, 6, cnt) == [ms[0], ms[2], ms[3]]
assert truncate_to_budget(ms, 100, cnt) == ms
assert truncate_to_budget(ms, 3, cnt) == [ms[0]]
m2 = [{"role":"system","content":"s"},{"role":"user","content":"a"},{"role":"user","content":"bbbbb"}]
assert truncate_to_budget(m2, 3, cnt) == [m2[0]]
reference:
def truncate_to_budget(messages, budget, count):
    sys_ = [m for m in messages if m['role'] == 'system']
    left = budget - sum(count(m) for m in sys_)
    keep = set()
    for i in range(len(messages) - 1, -1, -1):
        m = messages[i]
        if m['role'] == 'system': continue
        if count(m) > left: break
        left -= count(m); keep.add(i)
    return [m for i, m in enumerate(messages) if m['role'] == 'system' or i in keep]
